analysis:
The PR adds a client-side clusters-waitlist gate to the cluster onboarding. In ClusterSetupWizardCommand.swift, runOnboarding now calls requireNewPairApproval before onboardingSettings and before the instance lock is taken. The gate is skipped for request.scope == .localOnly and for any Mac whose ClusterPairSummary.local().paired is true or unreadable. Otherwise FeatureWaitlistGate.require() runs with the live access from the config path and a terminal confirm prompt. ClusterSetupCommand.swift and docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md only add help and doc text. The doc unit supplied (head lines 1320-1694) lies outside the changed range 49-75, so it holds no changed text.

Security view: this is a product-access (waitlist) gate, not an authorization or attestation control. It does not touch TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011 (App Attest or serving authorization), keys, encryption, prefix cache (T-041), or the wire protocol. The fail-open cases (already paired, unreadable pair state, local-only) are documented as intentional. Per the threat model, a local operator (ADV-001) controls the CLI, so a client gate can be bypassed by editing local state or the binary. The gate therefore must not be treated as enforcement; any real restriction on cluster serving through Darkbloom has to be enforced coordinator-side, which is platform-owned and out of scope here. I found no regression and no invalidated threat-model assumption.

Open integration questions, not findings: FeatureWaitlistGate, FeatureWaitlistAccess.live, SandboxTerminal.confirm and ClusterPairSummary.local were not in the supplied evidence. These are the network access and token handling for the waitlist call, error handling when offline, and how `paired` fails on unreadable state. Other entry points that start a pair (for example `darkbloom start` in a terminal) were not shown and may skip the gate. The threat model might note that the waitlist gate is advisory only.
